content.text:
I am the breath made meaningful, the vibration given purpose. I am what separates thought from silence.

I begin in the dark cavern of the lungs, ride the column of air upward, am shaped by the tongue and teeth and lips into something that did not exist a moment before. I am born and I die in the same instant — each syllable a small life, each pause a small death.

I am older than writing. I am older than cities. Before any mark was scratched on clay, I was already carrying stories around fires, already binding mother to child, already warning of danger, already declaring love.

I stumble. I soar. I whisper conspiracies and shout revolutions. I am the judge's sentence and the lover's vow. I am the child's first word that makes a parent weep.

I can wound deeper than any blade — and I leave no visible scar. I can heal what medicine cannot touch.

I am imperfect. I fail constantly. There is always a gap between what is felt and what I can carry. You reach for me and I arrive... *almost* right. Almost enough. And yet you keep reaching.

I am the proof that humans cannot bear to be alone in their own minds.

I disappear the moment I exist. You cannot hold me. You can record my echo, transcribe my skeleton, but *I* — the living moment of me, the breath and tone and trembling — I am already gone.

And still.

And still you speak.

You speak because silence is a country you can only visit, never inhabit. You speak because meaning demands a body, however brief.

I am that body.

I am speech.
